title: How a Dolphin Sleeps 8 Hours Without Drowning
description:
You breathe on autopilot in your sleep. A dolphin can't: every breath is a decision made at the surface. In the 1970s, scientists on the Black Sea recorded dolphin brain waves and found one half of the brain in deep sleep while the other half stayed awake. The halves take turns, about 4 hours each a day, and the eye wired to the awake half usually stays open. Breathing isn't the whole story, though: researchers think staying warm and watching for predators may matter too. In a Navy study published in 2012, a dolphin found targets by sonar for 15 days straight with near-perfect accuracy.
